title: Link-Time Bytecode Quickening for Java Card Virtual Machines Without Method-Component Expansion: A Formal and Analytical Study
abstract: Java Card virtual machines execute from non-volatile memory in secure elements, where repeated reference indirection adds latency to frequently executed instructions. This paper proposes link-time bytecode quickening for the statically resolvable invocation and static-field instructions: after the ordinary installation-time validation and symbolic resolution, the linker rewrites each selected three-byte instruction in place into an implementation-private direct-address form of the same length, an aligned opcode family carrying the three most significant bits, and the two operand bytes carrying the remaining sixteen bits of a 19-bit logical byte address, which covers 512 KiB above a platform constant. The eight opcode families are verified as available on four editions of the Java Card Virtual Machine Specification and are implemented in our Java Card operating system. A small-step operational semantics presents the standard and the quickened form of each instruction as two rules sharing one effect function, so that correctness reduces to address round-trip, address agreement at link time and per-family refinement obligations; single-step and execution equivalence are proved under explicit linker-correctness, address-stability, address-range and opcode-separation assumptions, and Method-component length and control-flow offsets are preserved. A parametric execution-cost model, instantiated on measured instruction profiles of two EMV applets, Visa VSDC 2.9.2 and the Mastercard M/Chip Advance applet, gives a modeled interpreter-time reduction of 7 to 11 percent relative to the standard implementation in the field. CAP-file input and application source code are preserved; a modified linker and interpreter are required, and invokevirtual and invokeinterface are excluded, since their targets are selected at execution time and cannot be bound by the linker.

title: Grid-Based Open-Land Solar Suitability Assessment of Bangladesh's Twelve City Corporations
abstract: Bangladesh's National Solar Energy Roadmap targets 40 GW of solar capacity by 2041, yet no existing study has quantified open-land solar potential at fine spatial resolution across the country's urban centers. This dataset contains all raw exports, processed CSV outputs, and analysis scripts (Google Earth Engine JavaScript and Python) used to assess open-land solar photovoltaic suitability across a uniform 1 km x 1 km grid (1,672 cells) spanning all twelve City Corporations of Bangladesh, using a hybrid multi-temporal satellite classification pipeline. The dataset includes hybrid open-land classification outputs, PVOUT extractions, slope-constraint data, road/power-line proximity data, and all Python/GEE scripts required to reproduce the analysis. See README.md for full documentation.

title: Logit-Aware MIMO AirComp for Distributed Mixture-of-Experts LLM Inference over Wireless Edge Networks
abstract: Distributed mixture-of-experts (MoE) inference is a promising architecture for deploying large language models (LLMs) at wireless edge networks because sparse experts can be placed across coordinated base stations (BSs), while the anchor node and user equipment (UE) can offload LLM inference tasks to BSs. The communication bottleneck is the MoE aggregation, where the anchor BS must recover a weighted sum of selected expert outputs before each decoding step. Over-the-air computation (AirComp) is well matched to this operation because the wireless multiple-access channel naturally superposes simultaneous transmissions. However, conventional AirComp minimizes communication distortion, whereas MoE aggregation errors have unequal impact on LLM outputs. We propose a logit-aware MIMO AirComp framework that estimates local logit sensitivity as block-level weights and jointly optimizes receive combiners and BS precoders under per-BS power constraints. We also develop an alternating algorithm that protects decoding decisions from aggregation perturbations. Using OpenCompass, we evaluate Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 on GSM8K and ARC-Challenge. At 30 dB aggregation SNR, perturbed Qwen3 retains 99.3% of clean GSM8K accuracy and 94.8% of clean ARC-Challenge accuracy. In a direct ARC-Challenge closed-loop audit over 295 examples, SW-AirComp achieves 43.73% accuracy at 30 dB and 26.78% at 20 dB, outperforming unweighted, matched-filter, and zero-forcing AirComp. In the wireless simulator, SW-AirComp reduces decision-relevant aggregation distortion; at 20 dB, its final weighted-sum mean-squared error is 53.5% lower than unweighted AirComp under the same channels, samples, and sensitivity weights. Logit-RMSE and logit-gap diagnostics further show that the gain comes from reducing output-logit perturbation and lowering the risk of top-token changes.

title: EADC: Evaluation of Advanced and Deep-level Compliance in Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been used in various industries. However, ensuring their compliance with complex laws and regulatory frameworks remains a great challenge. Existing evaluation paradigms mainly rely on static benchmarks that suffer from three severe limitations: First, the compliance rules being used do not comply with the requirements of Artificial Intelligence (AI) laws and regulations; Second, they only handle apparent, explicit compliance risks, leaving implicit and covert compliance risks undetected; Third, they fail to track the systematic propagation of risks along logical dependency chains or evaluate compliance within nuanced, context-based real-world scenarios. To bridge this critical gap, we introduce EADC, a novel advanced evaluation benchmark of LLMs based on an AI compliance knowledge graph and AI compliance legal experts. By mapping abstract legal rules into structured logical multi-relational graphs, our framework enables automated, evolving agents to distill and synthesize highly sophisticated adversarial scenarios. This compliance benchmark is reviewed and corrected by human AI legal experts throughout the whole process. The resulting dataset (4,435+ QA pairs) provides an extensive, multi-dimensional taxonomy covering critical regulatory frontiers, including bias and discrimination, fairness, personal privacy protection, and values. Crucially, our compliance dataset moves beyond shallow string-matching by incorporating contextual long-horizon interactions and logic-driven hazard chains, capturing deeply embedded compliance anomalies that bypass traditional filters. Experiment evaluations demonstrate that our framework exposes critical regulatory blind spots in state-of-the-art LLMs, offering a rigorous, AI laws and regulations-aligned benchmark to safeguard high-level and deep compliance in the application of LLMs.

title: Exponential Quantum Advantage in Testing Fourier Dimensionality
abstract: A boolean function $f$ has Fourier dimension $k$ if its nonzero Fourier coefficients span a subspace of dimension $k$. We consider the property testing task of determining whether a function has Fourier dimension at most $k$, or is $ε$-far from being so. We show that there is a $O(k/\sqrtε)$-query quantum property tester for this problem, which we show to be almost optimal. Combined with Gopalan et al.'s classical lower bound of $Ω(2^{k/2})$, this demonstrates an exponential quantum advantage for this task \cite{DBLP:journals/siamcomp/GopalanOSSW11}. We complement this result with a $\tilde{O}(2^{k/2}/ε)$ classical tester, giving a quadratic improvement over the previous best tester, and essentially settling the classical query complexity.

title: Dual Covariance Gaussian Splatting SLAM: Decoupling Rendering and Registration for Robust Real-Time Tracking
abstract: ICP-based 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) SLAM tracks in real time by registering incoming frames against map Gaussians, using each primitive's covariance for both rendering and registration. These two uses place conflicting demands on one covariance. The mapper shapes it to minimize photometric error, often flattening it against surfaces, while robust registration typically benefits from measurement uncertainty. We propose a dual-covariance parameterization. Each Gaussian keeps a single mean but holds two covariances: a rendering covariance optimized by the mapper, and a tracking covariance derived from an RGB-D sensor noise model. We further use the tracking covariances as Gaussian anchors for image corners, providing constraints in directions where depth geometry is weak. We evaluate on TUM RGB-D, ScanNet, Replica, and two outdoor sequences recorded with a RealSense D435i on wheeled and handheld platforms. We achieve robust tracking performance across multiple scenes and reduced odometry drift, while tracking at $\sim$ 60 FPS.

evidence.title: Dual Covariance Gaussian Splatting SLAM: Decoupling Rendering and Registration for Robust Real-Time Tracking
evidence.abstract: ICP-based 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) SLAM tracks in real time by registering incoming frames against map Gaussians, using each primitive's covariance for both rendering and registration. These two uses place conflicting demands on one covariance. The mapper shapes it to minimize photometric error, often flattening it against surfaces, while robust registration typically benefits from measurement uncertainty. We propose a dual-covariance parameterization. Each Gaussian keeps a single mean but holds two covariances: a rendering covariance optimized by the mapper, and a tracking covariance derived from an RGB-D sensor noise model. We further use the tracking covariances as Gaussian anchors for image corners, providing constraints in directions where depth geometry is weak. We evaluate on TUM RGB-D, ScanNet, Replica, and two outdoor sequences recorded with a RealSense D435i on wheeled and handheld platforms. We achieve robust tracking performance across multiple scenes and reduced odometry drift, while tracking at $\sim$ 60 FPS.

title: DO INFRASOUND ARRAYS HAVE AN ACCENT? VALIDATING AVALANCHE DETECTION ACROSS SITES AND WINTERS
abstract: Infrasound arrays may be used to monitor avalanches and other natural hazards, and machine learning classifiers can be used to discriminate event signals from other sources.Johnson et al. (ISSW 2024) showed that a classifier trained on one day of data from a station in Little Cottonwood Canyon could identify avalanches at a second station in the same canyon using waveform features alone.As these systems move toward deployment across new stations, seasons, and snow climates, we ask the degree to which we may trust them in deployment.Machine learning models are often opaque and strong aggregate metrics do not guarantee reliable behavior in the field.In this research we develop a cross-station, multi-season validation framework and test it across six deployment clusters in California, Colorado, Utah, Alaska, and New Zealand.A histogram gradient-boosted classifier reached avalanche window F1 = 0.942 in an 8-class model.A separate probe identified the receiving array from recordings of the same event heard on multiple arrays with balanced accuracy 0.565, compared with 0.333 by chance.Although array geometry features carried stronger station signature, they performed better than content features at two of three held-out sites.Thus, features with measurable station encoding (or "accent") did not always hurt performance at new sites.Replay on continuous data also showed that high event scores did not automatically become alarms under a given alert policy.The results support local calibration before deployment.

title: Holif-AM: high-order low information text filter for aero-space and military based on statistical evaluation and LLM fact-check
abstract: This era is characterized by information explosion and overload, with the aerospace and military fields being inundated with erroneous or ambiguous texts and documents. Some of these texts exhibit no obvious semantic flaws, feature sound structure, yet lack informativeness—making them difficult to filter. The term "high-order" is thus used to describe such texts appropriately. To eliminate high-order low-information texts and conserve engineers' attention, we propose the High-order Low-information Text Filter for Aerospace and Military (Holif-AM). This filter integrates statistical evaluation, large language model (LLM)-based fact-checking, and a newly introduced specialized dataset, namely the Space and Strategy Books (SSBooks). The quality ratings of 16 candidate texts from diverse sources generated by Holif-AM were highly consistent with manual evaluations: statistical evaluation ensured text stylistic consistency, while LLM-based fact-checking guaranteed factual accuracy. Furthermore, detailed analysis demonstrated that Holif-AM evaluates texts in an interpretable manner. In conclusion, the proposed method accurately filters high-order low-information texts in the aerospace and military context, thereby advancing real-world developments in this field. Additionally, by constructing datasets for other relevant fields, Holif-AM can be seamlessly generalized to other specialized domains.

title: Direct DC motor speed control using Soft Actor–Critic reinforcement learning
abstract: Accurate and robust speed regulation of direct-current (DC) motors is essential in industrial drive systems operating under load disturbances and parameter uncertainty. Conventional proportional–integral (PI) control remains widely adopted; however, its performance depends strongly on gain tuning and may degrade when operating conditions change. This paper proposes a Soft Actor–Critic (SAC) reinforcement learning controller for direct DC motor speed regulation, where the learned policy generates the armature voltage command without relying on a predefined PI structure. For benchmarking, a Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) agent is implemented to adaptively tune PI gains under identical simulation conditions, including the same motor model, sampling time, reference profile, disturbance scenarios, and reward formulation. Simulation results show that SAC achieves substantially faster transient performance, reducing peak time from 0.2648 s to 0.0790 s (70.2%) and settling time from 2.3376 s to 0.5698 s (75.6%), while reducing steady-state error from 0.04% to 0.0001% (99.75%). Robustness tests under severe load disturbance ( T L = 80 Nm), increased inertia (+30%), and increased armature resistance (+20%) confirm that SAC maintains closed-loop stability and rejects disturbances faster than the TD3-tuned PI baseline. These results highlight the effectiveness of entropy-regularized direct policy learning for high-performance DC motor speed regulation under uncertainty.

title: Synthesizing Proofs Using Proof Sharding and Exploration
abstract: Distributed systems are hard to implement correctly, and subtle bugs can go undetected using traditional testing. Formal verification offers an alternative for proving the correctness of complex distributed systems. Despite previous efforts to automate and facilitate formal verification, it is still hard to integrate formal verification in software development. Programmers need to query the theorem prover repeatedly to find the correct proof of their system. This cycle of going back and forth with the theorem prover involves a lot of human intervention and is a barrier to adopting formal verification in software development. In this paper, we address the challenges of scaling formal verification in practice by reducing the human intervention required to find the correctness proof of a distributed system. We propose ProofSaX, an automated tool that shards large verification tasks and explores the proof search space for each shard independently to synthesize correctness proofs. We use controlled exploration when adding possible proof annotations to handle the search-space explosion problem. We evaluate ProofSaX on a variety of safety proofs for distributed systems. We show that ProofSaX can find the last proof annotation in 86 out of 103 proof-completion tasks, with runtimes ranging from one minute to two hours.

title: CVaR anchor regression protects against rare shifts
abstract: We study prediction in new environments when training data contain rare, large shifts. Anchor regression penalizes the average of the squared mean residual across environments. It protects against shifts in an ellipsoid determined by the second moment of the training shifts. Covering rare shifts may therefore require a large penalty, expanding the ellipsoid in every direction and reducing accuracy on common environments. We propose CVaR anchor regression, which replaces the average of the squared mean residuals with a tail average. Unlike CVaR or GroupDRO applied directly to prediction risks, it does not give environments more weight solely because their noise levels are high. We prove an exact worst-case risk guarantee under a linear structural model that allows for heteroscedastic noise. For discrete environments, decreasing the CVaR tail fraction expands the robustness set from an ellipsoid to a scaled convex hull of the training shifts and their negatives. A separate parameter controls its scale. Examples show how the method can improve protection against rare shifts while retaining accuracy on common environments. We illustrate the method on New York City taxi data.

title: Knowledge-as-Skill: A Structural Design for Autonomous Knowledge-Base Use by LLM Agents
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) gives large language models (LLMs) access to external knowledge, but its conventional retrieve-concatenate-generate pipeline makes retrieval decisions on behalf of the model. As tool use and agent loops become more reliable, an agent can decide whether to retrieve, what to inspect, and when to stop. This shift exposes a new bottleneck: the agent may not know what a knowledge base contains. Traditional knowledge bases expose documents as anonymous text chunks with limited information about scope, purpose, provenance, or relations. We propose Knowledge-as-Skill, an organization scheme that makes a knowledge base discoverable, navigable, and self-descriptive. It has three layers: a discovery layer centered on SKILL.md; a navigation layer with one index.md per directory; and a knowledge layer containing documents with YAML frontmatter for topic, type, provenance, and lifecycle. The design follows the Open Knowledge Format (OKF) and the Skill protocol without modifying the agent framework. We also provide knowledge-as-skill, a pipeline for converting heterogeneous collections of PDFs, Word files, web exports, and notes into this structure. In a preliminary evaluation on the WixQA enterprise customer-support benchmark, our setup obtains 0.889 Factuality and 0.816 Context Recall, compared with reported Corpus2Skill values of 0.767 and 0.708. It obtains slightly lower Faithfulness, lower Context Precision, and more interaction turns. Because the models, prompts, and knowledge-package construction differ, these results are directional cross-work evidence rather than a controlled comparison.

title: Priority Claim: Individualized Semantic Reference Layers for Language Models
abstract: Andreas Ehstand is the author of a method in which a language model's own definitions serve as a reference layer, one person's differing meanings and decision reasons are elicited against it, stored as a versioned record, and used by later AI to continue that person's thinking. This public priority statement names the four elements of the method (model-generated reference layer; person-specific difference; persistent, versioned record; continuation by later AI) and lists the dated record of the author's work from 2025 onward, each entry with a third-party date (Zenodo, EUIPO, Internet Archive, Bitcoin blockchain). English and German versions included. title: ARI: Artificial Relational Intelligence. Module One: Measuring the Model, Ignoring the Relationship
abstract: The pursuit of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is organized almost exclusively around model capability and is measured through zero-state benchmark scoring an Artificial Intelligence (AI) system's first encounter with a task. This paper argues that capability on its own will not be the AI industry's deliverance. Benchmarked capability is largely decoupled from a user's experience of interaction value. This interaction value instead depends on contextual fit, how well a system's assistance matches this person's aims, situation, and ways of working, which is an outcome produced by the accumulated and person-specific context the system brings to this task. Put simply, we believe the “knowing and growing” alongside a user is more important to that user than an arbitrary benchmark score, which is a contour we find is ignored by current metrics. Fit is produced by person-specific state that accumulates over time, so instruments that evaluate models in a vacuum are, by default, blind to it. We term the layer that produces contextual fit Artificial Relational Intelligence (ARI). Our claim is not that intelligence is located in the relationship, but that a user's relationship with that intelligence is where this technology finds its higher purpose. While we offer suggestions for how this axis can be measured, our core argument is that the success of AI overall will depend on each system's deepening and evolving user relationships, rather than the fixation on the pursuit of general intelligence.

title: Training ML Models to Adapt at Test Time
abstract: Modern machine learning systems concentrate most of their computation beforedeployment and then use the resulting model as a fixed predictor. This design is brittle when deployment differs from training and poorly matched to difficult problems whose solution benefits from additional reasoning, feedback, or interaction after the input is known. This thesis studies a complementary paradigm: training models to use computation at test time as a means of adapting their behavior to the instance at hand. The central claim is that test-time computation should be understood as a learned adaptive procedure rather than simply a longer prediction. A useful procedure must decide which operations to perform, which information to seek, how to interpret intermediate feedback, and when further effort is worthwhile. For foundation models, these decisions form a sequential process that may include generation, verification, search, revision, and interaction. Learning such a process requires more than examples of successful final answers: it requires signals that distinguish operations that make genuine progress from those that merely resemble successful behavior. This perspective connects robustness under distribution shift with scalable reasoning. In both settings, a static predictor is limited by information unavailable during training, while adaptation can exploit evidence revealed at deployment. The thesis develops principles for constructing that evidence, assigning credit to intermediate decisions, and optimizing policies that use it. Structured assumptions and counterfactual data expose failure modes that ordinary training can overlook. Verification and outcome feedback provide scalable supervision, while reinforcement learning converts that supervision into adaptive behavior. The resulting procedures can improve with additional test-time compute, remain effective beyond the budgets seen during training, and allocate effort according to problem difficulty rather than spending a fixed amount on every instance. Across the theoretical analyses and empirical studies, three conclusions emerge. First, additional computation is valuable only when training rewards progress rather than length or superficial imitation. Second, the model's initialization acts as a prior over the adaptive procedures that learning can discover, so data, representation, and optimization must be designed together. Third, effective test-time adaptation depends on balancing exploration, exploitation, and information acquisition under a finite compute budget. These principles apply across robustness, mathematical reasoning, and interactive decision making, and suggest a path from fixed predictors toward systems that continue to learn how to solve a problem after it is presented."

title: Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant: Cross-Precision Output Divergence in LLM Inference
abstract: Greedy decoding from large language models is commonly treated as deterministic. We show it is not precision-invariant: the same model, prompt, and decoding algorithm produce different outputs in BF16 versus FP16 on identical hardware. Across our evaluations of six models (1.1B-7B parameters, four families; divergence additionally characterised at 12B) and three benchmarks, 49-100\% of prompts diverge; a single token flip often cascades into trajectory-level divergence. We develop an empirical error-propagation analysis and find that 22 layers of accumulated body error do not distinguish flipping from non-flipping steps; the outcome depends primarily on the top-two logit margin at the LM head relative to the directional perturbation between the top-two candidates. The analysis makes five testable predictions about intervention outcomes, including that applying more FP32 compute (broader scope) makes agreement worse. The experiments match all five predictions. The best-performing low-overhead intervention we evaluate, selective FP32 LM head recomputation, triggered only when the margin falls below a threshold, delivers +22-36 pp exact agreement on A10G (+12-21 pp on L4 and A100) at less than 4\% latency overhead in low-batch (batch size <=4) single-stream inference. We map the applicability boundary across six models and four batch sizes, and hypothesise that training-time precision stability is a determining factor. The method is a partial mitigation rather than a universal determinism guarantee: its benefit vanishes when body-originated error dominates, including at batch size >=8 and under end-to-end FP8 in our tests.

title: SAMI3D-DW: Interactive Segmentation of Any 3D Medical Images
abstract: Interactive segmentation of 3D medical images supports quantitative analysis of anatomical structures and disease while allowing users to specify and refine their targets. Despite substantial progress by nnInteractive and VISTA3D, reliable segmentation across diverse clinical targets remains challenging, particularly for complex anatomical structures and the heterogeneous, long-tailed spectrum of pathology. We present SAMI3D-DW V1 (hereafter SAMI3D-DW), an interactive 3D segmentation model trained on Deepwise's large-scale proprietary medical image datasets. We evaluate the model under simulated user interactions on a CT/MR benchmark comprising 4,326 cases from 219 source datasets, spanning 107 anatomical and pathological categories, organized by a medical taxonomy and evaluated with a category-balanced DSC score. SAMI3D-DW achieves the highest category-macro Dice among evaluated methods in both interaction modes. With one point, it scores 0.5756 versus 0.5316 for nnInteractive, the strongest baseline, rising to 0.7771 versus 0.7495 with five points. With bounding-box initialization, the scores are 0.7129 versus 0.6530. After five corrective clicks, SAMI3D-DW reaches 0.8004 versus 0.7868. For radiologists and clinicians, SAMI3D-DW enables segmentation of complex anatomical structures, including intracranial vessel trees on CT and MR angiography, with a few clicks. evidence.title: SAMI3D-DW: Interactive Segmentation of Any 3D Medical Images
evidence.abstract: Interactive segmentation of 3D medical images supports quantitative analysis of anatomical structures and disease while allowing users to specify and refine their targets. Despite substantial progress by nnInteractive and VISTA3D, reliable segmentation across diverse clinical targets remains challenging, particularly for complex anatomical structures and the heterogeneous, long-tailed spectrum of pathology. title: Evaluating Multilingual Ordinal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis and Sarcasm Detection under Distribution Shift: The VN-MSASar Hospitality Benchmark
abstract: VN-MSASar is an aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) dataset for the hotel and restaurant domain in Vietnam, covering four languages (Vietnamese, English, Chinese, Japanese). Version 3 contains 76,785 (sentence, aspect) pairs drawn from 18,609 reviews over nine service aspects, each with an ordinal sentiment label on a [-3,+3] scale and a binary sarcasm label. Every row is a real review. The 7,659 synthetic, template-generated sentences that formed the "augmented" source in version 1 have been removed. Splitting moved from the sentence to the review, so no review appears in two splits, and near-duplicate leakage was audited under a two-part criterion (TF-IDF character 3-5-gram cosine, or character-4-gram containment) that reports zero flagged pairs between train and either evaluation split. Results computed on version 1 are not comparable to version 3. This record contains the main aspect-pair version (vn_msa_sar_v3) with fixed train/validation/test splits of 60,406 / 8,152 / 8,227 rows. Columns: review_id, source, place_type, language, sentence, aspect, sentiment, sarcasm. A derived multi-label aspect-detection version can be reconstructed by pivoting on the aspect column. Reporting note. The "other" source is a deliberate over-sample of sarcastic reviews (2,375 rows, all sarcastic, distributed 70/15/15 by near-duplicate cluster). Primary results should be reported on the natural slice test[source != "other"], which matches the deployment distribution; the full test set is for sarcasm analysis, where the larger positive class gives tighter confidence intervals. Labels were produced by a two-step LLM pipeline. Human validation of the sentiment labels was carried out on version 1; re-validation on version 3, covering aspect labels as well, is in preparation and will be added in a subsequent version of this record. See README.md in the archive for the full schema, composition tables, leakage verification and known limitations.

title: Quantum Teleportation Over 1,400 km: State Transfer, Not Matter, via Entanglement — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Quantum teleportation transmits state information (not matter) over 1,400 km via entanglement, with no classical speed limit violation; the "trick" is that the state is destroyed at source and recreated at destination, requiring classical communication (≤c) to complete. | MATH: Teleportation fidelity \(F = \text{Tr}(\rho_{\text{out}}\rho_{\text{in}})\); for ideal Bell-state measurement, \(F=1\). Entanglement resource: Bell pair \(|\Phi^+\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|00\rangle+|11\rangle)\). Total state after joint measurement: \(|\psi\rangle_{\text{in}} \otimes |\Phi^+\rangle_{AB} \rightarrow \sum_{i=0}^3 |\Phi_i\rangle_{A} \otimes (\sigma_i |\psi\rangle)_B\), where \(\sigma_i \in \{I, \sigma_x, \sigma_y, \sigma_z\}\) (Pauli rotations). Classical bits required: 2 (log₂4). No equation for distance; 1,400 km is an experimental parameter (satellite link, Micius). | CONNECTION: The four Bell states form a basis isomorphic to the Klein four-group \(Z_2 \times Z_2\), whose character Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Dataset and Experimental Results: Robust Aggregation Ranks the Free-Rider First
abstract: Prototype-based federated learning exchanges class-embedding matrices without exposing the computation that produced them. We evaluate three verification mechanisms against free-riding at this interface: robust aggregation used for contribution ranking, commitments to model behavior, and passport-derived identities. On CIFAR-100, Krum assigns a client that republishes the aggregate a detection AUC of 0.011, and distances from coordinate-wise median, trimmed-mean and Bulyan outputs yield 0.000. Exact score comparisons explain this inversion, and a matched-moment counterexample shows that no criterion based on the cohort mean and scalar dispersion can predict it. A prover with no model or data passes all 40 rounds of a behavioral-commitment verifier. In the passport installation map studied, 98.21% of passport dimensions lie in a nullspace and normalization adds a rescaling invariance, so one model yields many identities without establishing admission to a permissioned federation. A payload auditor over signed history detects six non-adaptive replay attacks across five held-out seeds, but also flags the honest client whose payload is copied, detects reduced training effort weakly, and is evaded by an attacker that evaluates its score. The results separate payload consistency, model identity and evidence that training occurred. Dataset Content: This repository contains the supplementary data and experimental assets to support and reproduce the results presented in the paper. Specifically, this dataset includes: Evaluation Results: The measured results supporting every table and figure in the manuscript, provided in JSON format. Archived Trajectories: Archived prototype trajectories that support the detector replay analyses. Model Checkpoints: Saved model checkpoints used for the passport-map measurements and inverse verifications.

title: A node-centric artificial bee colony framework for dominating tree construction
abstract: Abstract Designing efficient communication backbones is crucial for modern network applications, such as wireless sensor networks & multicast routing, and the dominating tree problem (DTP) was formulated by keeping these applications in mind. The DTP is an NP -hard problem that involves constructing a tree in a connected, edge-weighted, undirected graph with the aim of minimizing the total edge cost while ensuring that every vertex is either part of the tree or adjacent to a vertex in the tree. This paper presents a node-based artificial bee colony (ABC) framework for the DTP, which incorporates problem-specific variation operators designed to effectively navigate the solution space. Unlike most previous approaches for DTP, which focus on selecting edges, the proposed ABC framework first selects the nodes and then constructs the minimum spanning tree over the subgraph induced by selected nodes and a few additional nodes lying on the shortest paths joining pairs of selected nodes. The proposed ABC framework is tested on standard benchmark instances and results are compared with those of the best performing methods in the literature. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The proposed ABC framework obtained solutions as good as or better than the best performing methods on a large majority of instances. The proposed algorithm also enhanced the best known results for three benchmark instances.

title: Hi-SCCG: Hierarchical Structure-aware Chunking and Context Generation for document-level information extraction
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based generative Information Extraction (IE) over long documents is constrained by finite context windows, and the necessary text-chunking step disrupts semantic continuity, causing subject drift, unresolved coreference, and loss of the global constraints required for fine-grained knowledge graph construction. Existing context-augmentation methods either provide only limited local context or incur substantial computational cost while introducing irrelevant information, largely because they do not fully exploit document hierarchy. We propose Hi-SCCG (Hierarchical Structure-aware Chunking and Context Generation), a framework that models document structure by reconstructing the logical skeleton as a semantic tree through LLM-based heading correction and by generating cached multi-granularity summaries with a bottom-up recursive strategy. During inference, Hi-SCCG injects a lightweight path-aware context formed by concatenating ancestor summaries from the leaf chunk to the document root, thereby helping anchor local text to its document-level and section-level subjects. We further introduce LDE-500, a focused benchmark for document-level IE over Chinese hierarchical documents, and use Subject Restoration Rate (SRR) as a diagnostic subset-recall measure for triples that require subject restoration. On LDE-500, Hi-SCCG achieves an F1-score of 0.82 and a diagnostic SRR of 82.1%, with a 9.4 percentage-point absolute SRR improvement over the strongest evaluated baseline. In a representative token-accounting case involving a 45K-token document, after including one-time heading correction, recursive summary-generation calls, extraction input tokens, and extraction output tokens, Hi-SCCG reduces total KG-construction token consumption by 75.4–77.7% relative to SLIDE. These results suggest that structure-aware path injection is a promising strategy for fine-grained IE in structure-rich long documents when SRR is interpreted together with standard triple-level metrics and subset-level precision. A supplementary fully human-annotated Legal-OOD-60 evaluation shows a similar trend in this compact legal-domain sample, where Hi-SCCG achieves an F1-score of 0.77 and an SRR of 75.0%, although broader cross-domain validation remains necessary.

title: An Exponential Succinctness Gap between Three-Variable Logic and the Calculus of Relations
abstract: Three-variable first-order logic (FO3) and the calculus of relations (CoR) define the same binary queries, an equivalence going back to Tarski in the 1940s. While the classical translation $\text{FO3} \Rightarrow \text{CoR}$ is exponential, we prove that this blow-up is unavoidable, resolving a long-standing open question. We construct positive formulas $φ$ with a single quantifier whose equivalent terms require size $2^{Ω(|φ|)}$, even over finite structures and circuit representations with subterm sharing. Our proof uses a preservation argument over a single finite structure. This approach applies beyond our primary question, establishing the lower bound even for size-specific circuits and bounded-error randomized circuits, and yielding an analogous exponential gap for the matrix query language MATLANG.

title: GeoComposer: Geometry-Grounded Photographic Composition Instruction
abstract: Photographic composition aims to provide visual guidance for improving the framing, viewpoint, and spatial arrangement of an image. Early methods primarily rely on image cropping to enhance composition, which is restricted to the viewpoint and spatial arrangement of the input image. Recent methods have explored image understanding and editing to improve composition, but they mainly focus on instruction following and aesthetic quality, overlooking the importance of 3D scene geometry consistency for photographic composition. In this work, we propose GeoComposer, a novel geometry-grounded photographic composition framework that analyzes the composition of a given image to generate textual guidance and synthesizes a visual exemplar that enhances the composition of the given image. To promote geometry-grounded composition, we propose a geometry-aware representation learning mechanism that leverages geometric priors from a visual geometry foundation model to shape the intermediate representations of the composition editing model. This mechanism preserves both global structural relationships and local fine-grained correspondences for geometry-grounded composition. Furthermore, we propose a reinforcement learning strategy guided by a hybrid reward that jointly optimizes instruction following, aesthetic quality, and geometric consistency. This enables the model to generate visual exemplars that faithfully follow the composition instructions while remaining visually appealing and geometrically consistent. Extensive experiments show the superiority of our approach over state-of-the-art methods, highlighting its effectiveness in generating visually appealing and geometrically consistent composition.

title: EMERGE: Resolution-Agnostic Point Cloud Generation with Equivariant Graph-Based Diffusion
abstract: Point cloud generation has emerged as a crucial task for accurately capturing and reproducing the complexity of the physical world. However, existing generative approaches, predominantly relying on Transformers and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), frequently ignore the continuous, non-grid topologies inherent to 3D spaces. Although the integration of graph-based structures has yielded significant benefits in related discriminative vision tasks, such geometric architectures remain noticeably absent from 3D generative modeling. To address this gap, we introduce EMERGE (Equivariant Multi-scale GNN for Resolution-agnostic point cloud GEneration), the first fully $SE(3)$-equivariant graph-based diffusion backbone explicitly designed to generate point clouds while preserving continuous spatial symmetries. Our framework bypasses the rigid resolution dependencies of standard generative pipelines, enabling zero-shot inference at multiple, arbitrary spatial resolutions. Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that EMERGE achieves State-of-the-Art generation quality across standard metrics, while the strong inherent geometric inductive biases enable significantly faster training convergence compared to existing baseline methods.

title: The Failure of Simultaneous Quantum Typicality
abstract: We establish exact thresholds for the failure of simultaneous quantum typicality: three parties for mixed states and four for pure states. For the four-qubit Higuchi--Sudbery state, every sequence satisfying the expected purity bounds on three overlapping marginals, with sufficiently small fixed positive entropy slack, is asymptotically perfectly distinguishable from the tensor powers of the input: its trace distance from them tends to the maximum value $2$. This maximal separation persists, with a common positive slack, throughout an open neighborhood in the full four-qubit state space. Tracing out one party yields a mixed tripartite example. The proof connects simultaneous quantum smoothing with polynomial concentration on $\CP^1$. Symmetry reduces the problem to a frame inequality on $\Sym^n(\mathbb C^2)$, where a linear entropy deficit competes with a quadratic cost of polynomial concentration. Bernstein--Markov estimates and a subharmonic barrier control this cost, yielding an exponential obstruction to simultaneous typicality. These results disprove Dutil's multiparty quantum typicality conjecture, formulated in 2011, and the one-shot simultaneous min-entropy-smoothing conjectures of Drescher--Fawzi and Colomer--Winter. Together with the positive results for smaller systems, they determine the smallest numbers of parties at which simultaneous typicality can fail.

title: SUN'IY INTELLEKTDAN FOYDALANISHDAGI YUTUQLAR VA MUAMMOLAR
abstract: Ushbu maqolada sun'iy intellekt (SI) texnologiyalaridan turli sohalarda foydalanishning zamonaviy holati, erishilgan yutuqlar va yuzaga kelayotgan muammolar ilmiy jihatdan tahlil qilinadi. Sog‘liqni saqlash, ta'lim, sanoat va davlat boshqaruvi sohalarida SI qo‘llanilishining ijobiy natijalari, shuningdek ish o‘rinlarining qisqarishi, algoritmik xolislik (bias), maxfiylik, noto‘g‘ri ma'lumotlarning tarqalishi va energiya-ekologik yuk kabi muammolar xalqaro tadqiqot va statistik ma'lumotlar (Stanford AI Index, McKinsey, PwC, IEA, Pew Research, UNDP) asosida yoritiladi. O‘zbekiston Respublikasida sun'iy intellekt sohasini rivojlantirish bo‘yicha qabul qilingan strategik hujjatlar ham ko‘rib chiqiladi. Maqolaning asosiy qismida har bir aniqlangan muammoga nisbatan xalqaro amaliyotda sinovdan o‘tgan aniq yechimlar (huquqiy tartibga solish, texnik vositalar, tashkiliy chora-tadbirlar) taklif etiladi.

title: Xeno Coefficient v0.6 — Experimental Result: The RF-BLOCK Bottleneck after Five Operational Atlases: A 100-Condition Diagnostic Synthesis
abstract: This paper presents a governed diagnostic synthesis of the first five closed Xeno Coefficient v0.6 Operational Atlases, covering Applications 01–25 and exactly one hundred prospectively frozen 1300-token conditions measured under the unchanged released R2_LTR96/TP operational specification, in order to identify which component of the post-release decision architecture has most consistently prevented numerically substantial conditions from reaching causal-historical support while explicitly refusing to treat the accumulated record as a retrospective calibration population, threshold-search space, receiver-redesign opportunity, or justification for modifying any frozen component of v0.6. Across the one hundred conditions, ninety-seven yield numeric-complete coefficients while three remain legitimately numeric-incomplete under the frozen R_G^F Primary/Holdout collapse law, complete-condition xi_0.6^TP has mean 67.353476975634 and median 67.248087858176, mean reportable R_G^F is 0.301602166878, mean V_TP across all conditions is 0.739005979023, zero conditions reach C_H=Supported, zero evaluable conditions become candidate-positive, and all four hundred C7/C8 first-64 median RF-BLOCK total-variation observations remain below the frozen 0.05 threshold, with range 0.003215900719–0.016777274748, mean 0.009433489398, and median 0.009255348706. Because Counterfactual Precision remains internally heterogeneous across STABLE-PASS, STABLE-FAIL, and INDETERMINATE-PRECISION states, because numerous conditions reach five or six of eight causal-history criteria, and because complete coefficient formation remains overwhelmingly successful, the cumulative field does not support an interpretation of general measurement failure but instead localizes the dominant observed constraint at the RF-BLOCK historical-effect magnitude layer, where C7 and C8 repeatedly prevent progression to C_H=Supported despite substantial numerical coefficients and partially successful upstream criteria. This four-hundred-of-four-hundred recurrence is therefore fixed as a descriptive bottleneck rather than a recalibration result, and it does not authorize lowering the 0.05 threshold, modifying RF-BLOCK B=8, rescuing missing coefficients, changing R2_LTR96, retrospectively reclassifying prior measurements, or altering any other part of the released v0.6 specification, while providing a clearly defined target for any future prospectively governed validation program investigating receiver sensitivity, perturbation design, block size, effect-magnitude estimation, or threshold behavior.

title: Data and code for "Residual information and the limits of risk certification in finite budget zero noise extrapolation"
abstract: This deposit contains simulation data, research code, and reproduction instructions supporting the manuscript “Residual information and the limits of risk certification in finite budget zero noise extrapolation” by Zheng Chen. The materials concern finite-budget zero-noise extrapolation, pilot-conditional risk certification, pilot reuse, partial extrapolation, and calibration costs. The records consist entirely of numerical simulations and do not contain quantum-hardware measurements, human-subject data, personal data, or confidential institutional data. Both favorable and unfavorable results are retained. The package includes response catalogs, scenario definitions, per-repetition records, numerical summaries, figure source data, finite-calibration records, research software, integrity manifests, and reproduction instructions. Internal review documents, submission correspondence, local workflow records, credentials, and third-party article excerpts are excluded. The study identifies conditions and limitations of risk certification. It does not establish a generally superior quantum error-mitigation algorithm or a cost-effective procedure for acquiring all required residual information. OpenAI Codex assisted with derivations, simulation code, analysis, literature work, plotting, and manuscript preparation. Separate AI sessions provided internal computational checks, not external peer review. The author remains responsible for the deposited materials and associated research claims.

title: FedMAST: Backdoor Detection and Containment in Federated Learning
abstract: FedMAST is the reproducibility artifact for the paper Backdoors Leave Structural Traces: FedMAST for Backdoor Detection and Containment in Federated Learning, accepted at the 38th IEEE International Conference on Tools with Artificial Intelligence (ICTAI 2026). The artifact contains the Flower-based federated learning simulation used for the reported CIFAR-10 experiments, including the FedMAST defense, its 22 structural features and six spectral-drift features, thresholding and consensus logic, cluster bisection, anchor-based validation, coalition re-sorting, containment, quarantine, and historical state tracking. The repository also includes implementations and experiment support for Constrain-and-Scale, Neurotoxin, LGA, DBA, 3DFed, BC-Layers, and the adaptive CovertLayers attack, together with FedAvg, Multi-Krum, Trimmed Mean, FLAME, and AlignIns baselines.

title: Loss Choice or Model Choice? The Role of Forecast Level in Cryptocurrency Volatility Forecasting
abstract: Volatility forecasts play a central role in financial risk management because their overall level and day-to-day movements affect downstream decisions. Most studies compare forecasting models while keeping the training loss fixed. Yet losses emphasise different errors and can target different properties of future volatility, so raw comparisons may combine persistent forecast-level differences with differences in daily forecast movements. This leaves unresolved whether the importance of loss choice comes mainly from the forecast level it targets or from differences that remain after level adjustment. We address this gap through a comparison of seven losses and five models across major cryptocurrencies. Validation-based alignment adjusts the forecast level before the raw and aligned forecasts are evaluated using statistical scores and one-day Value-at-Risk. Before alignment, marginal score variation is greater across losses. After alignment, model choice becomes the larger source of variation in the full five-model comparison, while cross-loss differences in VaR breach rates narrow substantially. Our contribution is a comprehensive evaluation of loss and model choice that shows why losses can appear so influential in raw comparisons and how this interpretation changes when forecast level and downstream risk are considered explicitly.

title: MMAP: Multimodal Missing-Aware Pretraining for Longitudinal Alzheimer's Prediction
abstract: Clinical decision making heavily relies on predicting the disease progression trajectory by seeking to understand patient's health status which is characterised by multimodal medical data. AI holds great potential for learning useful representations from multimodal medical data to predict disease progression and aid clinical decision making. However, development of predictive AI models is constrained by missing modalities and incomplete tabular data frequently occurring in medical datasets. In addition, disease labels alone may only provide limited supervisory signals for learning representations from high-dimensional multimodal data. Here, we present MMAP, a novel Multimodal Missing-aware Alignment Pretraining method for learning image-tabular representations from incomplete data. An image encoder is pretrained with efficient sigmoid contrastive learning combined with generative reconstruction. A tabular encoder is built upon a tabular foundation model. A missing token generator enables the two encoders to take incomplete data as input, enabling the model to be robust against missing modalities, either with missing images or missing tabular data. We evaluate the clinical usefulness of the learnt multimodal representations on two challenging longitudinal clinical tasks for Alzheimer's disease: predicting disease stage conversion and predicting amyloid status. The proposed method outperforms strong multimodal and unimodal baselines.

title: Maximum-Likelihood Amplitude Estimation for Quantum Monte Carlo Integration on Trapped-Ion Hardware: Convergence, Noise-Floor Saturation, Depth-Dependent Bias
abstract: Quantum Amplitude Estimation promises to accelerate Monte Carlo integration by replacing the classical $\varepsilon \propto N^{-1/2}$ sampling law with the Heisenberg-limited $\varepsilon \propto N^{-1}$ scaling, but whether any part of that advantage survives on present-day hardware is an empirical question. We report a systematic experimental benchmark of a Maximum-Likelihood Amplitude Estimation QMC pipeline on IonQ trapped-ion processors, comprising 60 hardware trials on IonQ Forte-1 across five settings(5 & 9 qubits, 100-200 shots per depth, linear & exponential amplification schedules, ~113 device-hours), together with 100 trials on IonQ Aria-1 & Forte-1 noise models at 5, 9 & 19 qubits. The pipeline combines controlled-$R_y$ rotational state preparation, Grover-based amplitude amplification and maximum-likelihood inference and is benchmarked against $b_{\max}^{-1}\!\int_0^{b_{\max}}\!\sin^2\!x\,\mathrm{d}x$ with $b_{\max}=π/5$ ,given results emerge. First, the noiseless limit it attains $\varepsilon \propto N^{-0.88}$, close to the Heisenberg-scaling reference, reducing the error 54-74x over a 133x increase in oracle calls. Second, scaling does not survive on hardware. Every noisy backend saturates at an error floor of (2-5)x 10^{-2}, with fitted exponents of 0.04-0.15 on Forte-1 linear schedules and $α\le\!0$ on the vendor noise models: beyond the optimal shallow depth, however, deeper amplification provides no sustained accuracy gain and instead returns to the noise floor. Forte-1 hardware also outperformed IonQ's own Aria-1 noise model at every depth $m \ge 2$, indicating that vendor noise models are bad predictors of MLAE accuracy. The practical implication for UQ is that on current devices the useful operating point is a shallow, schedule-tuned amplification depth chosen so that the deepest circuit lands near p~1/2 not the deepest schedule the coherence budget allows.

title: Analysis of the effectiveness of LLM in processing public procurement tender documentation
abstract: Razpisna dokumentacija javnih naročil lahko vsebuje veliko informacij, ki so razdeljene med več različnih dokumentov. Njihovo iskanje in pravilno razumevanje je zato lahko časovno potratno. Namen diplomske naloge je raziskati uporabnost velikih jezikovnih modelov pri obravnavi razpisne dokumentacije javnih naročil. V nalogi so predstvaljene osnovne zmožnosti in omejitve umetne inteligence, velikih jezikovnih modelov, ter pristopa generiranja z razširjenim iskanjem (angl. retrieval-augmented generation, RAG). Poleg tega so predstavljene tudi značilnosti javnih naročil in razpisne dokumentacije. Osrednji del naloge predstavlja analiza učinkovitosti velikih jezikovnih modelov pri izpolnjevanju razpisne dokumentacije. Raziskava je bila izvedena z osmimi udeleženci, razdeljenimi v dve skupini. Ena skupina je vprašanja reševala z uporabo velikega jezikovnega modela, druga pa brez njegove uporabe. Primerjani so bili čas reševanja, pravilnost odgovorov in opažanja udeležencev. Udeleženci z uporabo velikega jezikovnega modela so vprašalnik v povprečju rešili hitreje in dosegli večjo pravilnost odgovorov. Tudi njihova opažanja kažejo na enostavnejše iskanje informacij. Rezultati kažejo, da so veliki jezikovni modeli lahko uporabno podporno orodje pri obravnavi razpisne dokumentacije. Kljub temu je pomembno, da uporabnik pridobljene informacije preveri v izvorni dokumentaciji in ohrani končno presojo.

title: Disseny i desenvolupament d un middleware de privacitat basat en la desidentificació semàntica per a la interacció segura amb models de llenguatge
abstract: [ES] Este trabajo presenta AXION, un middleware de privacidad diseñado para la interacción segura con Modelos de Lenguaje Grandes (LLM). Cuando un usuario envía texto a un LLM externo (OpenAI, Google Gemini), cualquier dato personal contenido en el prompt abandona su red local, lo que genera un riesgo directo de incumplimiento del Reglamento General de Protección de Datos (RGPD). AXION resuelve este problema mediante una capa de desidentificación local que intercepta las peticiones antes de su transmisión. El sistema emplea un pipeline híbrido de cuatro capas: (1) expresiones regulares determinis tas para datos estructurados (DNI, IBAN, correo electrónico), (2) el modelo Transformer Ettin-68M-Nemotron-PII de 68 millones de parámetros para reconocimiento de entida des semánticas, (3) un corrector ortográfico (pyspellchecker) para detectar disparado res sensibles con errores tipográficos, y (4) un analizador de dependencias gramaticales Sujeto-Verbo-Objeto (SVO) basado en spaCy, que diferencia entre divulgación personal («Vivo en Madrid») y consulta funcional («Clima en Madrid»). La arquitectura sigue los principios de Clean Architecture, implementada con FastAPI, LangChain (LCEL) y un almacenamiento efímero de sesiones en RAM con aislamiento por hilos. La validación empírica sobre 1000 muestras del dataset Ai4Privacy-300K demuestra un recall de 1.00 para correos electrónicos, 0.88 para localizaciones y 0.78 para nombres, con una latencia agregada del pipeline de 21.67 ms en CPU sin GPU. Una auditoría cruzada contra WikiANN cuantifica la brecha de generalización —el recall de localizaciones se degrada sobre texto natural—, mientras que la capa determinista preserva la cobertura de los identificadores estructurados con independencia del dominio. El sistema se despliega mediante Docker Compose y soporta los idiomas inglés y español sin penalización de latencia.

title: KI-Nutzung in deutschen Aufsichtsräten : Ein Survey zu aktuellen Potentialen und Hemmnissen sowie Zukunftsperspektiven
abstract: Darüber hinaus arbeitet die Studie Verhaltens-und Interaktionsmuster im Zusammenspiel von Corporate Governance, Führung und KI heraus.In Anlehnung an die qualitative Vorstudie werden Parallelen und Abweichungen systematisch betrachtet, um ein differenziertes Bild der heutigen Praxis und der nächsten sinnvollen Schritte zu zeichnen.Zwischen Kontrolle und Potential: Künstliche Intelligenz als neuer Akteur im Aufsichtsrat Methode: Die Datenerhebung erfolgt über einen strukturierten Online-Fragebogen, der standardisierte Messinstrumente (siehe dazu die Fußnoten auf den entsprechenden Folien) auf Basis von Likert-Skalen sowie eigens entwickelte Fragemodule umfasst, welche aus der qualitativen Vorstudie abgeleitet wurden.Zielgruppe: Aufsichtsratsmitglieder deutscher Aktiengesellschaften Stichprobe: Das Gesamtsample (N = 103) setzt sich aus Aufsichtsratsmitgliedern deutscher Aktiengesellschaften zusammen, die über verschiedene Online-Kanäle angesprochen wurden (nicht repräsentative Selbstrekrutierung). Insgesamt verteilen sich die Aufsichtsratsmitglieder zu rund 21% auf DAX, zu 23% auf MDAX, zu 34% auf SDAX und zu 21% auf Andere.Die jeweilige Sample-Größe kann aufgrund einer Mehrfachauswahl bei einzelnen Fragen variieren.Die Kontaktaufnahme zu Aufsichtsräten erfolgt über Institutionen wie den Verband Frauen in die Aufsichtsräte e.V. (FidAR), die Regierungskommission Deutscher Corporate Governance Kodex (DCGK), die Hans-Böckler-Stiftung sowie das Frankfurt School Forum.Eine weitere Kontaktaufnahme erfolgt über Aufsichtsratsgruppen innerhalb des beruflichen Online-Netzwerkes LinkedIn.Im Zuge dessen erfolgt zudem die individuelle Kontaktaufnahme von über 300 Aufsichtsräten deutscher Aktiengesellschaften des DAX, MDAX, SDAX und Anderer über das Online-Netzwerk LinkedIn.Themenbereiche: Demografische und allgemeine Informationen, Unternehmenskontext, Persönliche Interaktion mit KI, Derzeitige Nutzung von KI im Aufsichtsrat, Zukünftige Veränderungen durch KI, Hindernisse für den Einsatz von KI, Einstellung gegenüber KI, Allgemeine ethische Fragen zum Einsatz

title: Stability-Aware Auditing of Latent Regions in Sentence Embedding Spaces: Guarding Against Granularity Collapse in Unsupervised Text Analytics
abstract: Sentence-embedding clustering is often interpreted from a single partition, although a reproducible solution can still be excessively coarse, cardinality-variable, or representation-dependent. We present a stability-aware audit framework that separates label-free operating-point selection from post hoc taxonomy evaluation and explicitly distinguishes the original frozen confirmatory execution from separately frozen additional robustness analyses. On a pinned Banking77 test revision (N=3076) and CLINC150+OOS (N=5500), the original anti-collapse rule selected seven-region MeanShift operating points with disjoint-random-stream confirmation ARIs of 0.9565±0.0510 and 0.9347±0.0327, respectively. Additional paired refits showed that rejected coarse candidates can remain more stable than the selected solutions, and this stability–granularity inversion persisted under ARI, AMI, NMI, V-measure, and Fowlkes–Mallows similarity. The additional audits also showed that high membership similarity can coexist with refit-cardinality variation, that representation and broader pipeline perturbations materially affect the discovered structure, and that density-based stability must be interpreted jointly with coverage and cardinality. These results support a conservative conclusion: perturbation stability is evidence of reproducibility under a stated protocol, not proof of an appropriate resolution, semantic validity, or taxonomy recovery.

title: Adversarial Attacks and Identity Leakage in De-Identification Systems: An Empirical Study
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the impact of adversarial attacks on identity encoders within a realistic de-identification framework. Our experiments show that the transferability of attacks transfers from an external surrogate model to the system model (e.g., CosFace to ArcFace) allows the adversary to cause identity information to leak in a sufficiently sensitive face recognition system. We present experimental evidence and propose strategies to mitigate this vulnerability. Specifically, we show how fine-tuning on adversarial examples helps to mitigate this effect for distortion-based attacks (i.e., snow, fog, etc.), while a simple low-pass filter can attenuate the effect of adversarial noise without affecting the de-identified images. Our mitigation results in a de-identification system that preserves its functionality while being significantly more robust to adversarial noise.

title: Semantic Abstraction for Natural Language Inference: a Methodological Framework for Discovering and Compensating Semantic Knowledge and Reasoning Gaps in Large Language Models
abstract: Despite their outstanding performance on many NLP tasks, LLMs face serious challenges related to semantic abstraction. In this study, we are interested in understanding how LLMs leverage abstract semantic knowledge in natural language inference (NLI), which requires sophisticated linguistic capabilities to interpret implicit meanings, contextual conceptual relationships, and semantic connections between words and phrases. To this end, we propose a methodological framework for constructing new semantic knowledge at a higher level of abstraction, which we define under the notions of semantic compatibility and incompatibility for NLI. In this framework, the meaning of the lexical-semantic relations between the premise and the hypothesis is reconfigured to achieve a more flexible semantic network that induces different reasoning paths in LLMs. These new pathways show a consistent pattern of responses that allows agreement on a single response. The results demonstrate that our proposal allows to discover and compensate for LLMs' semantic knowledge gaps in NLI, achieving significant improvements in accuracy, exceeding 10% for some models, and in particular for the non-entailment class. It is essential to note that LLMs need structured knowledge and not just more data to bridge reasoning gaps. Our hybrid approach directs attention to overlooked word relationships, allowing models to synthesize missing information. We believe that the future lies not in increasing model size, but in creating a semantic scafolding that mimics the flexibility of human thinking. Hopefully, our proposal will enable the development of more robust agents and interpretable reasoning, guiding AI toward reliable language understanding.

title: Birleştirilmiş ve çoklu imza şemalarında yerel doğrulanabilirlik: eşleme tabanlı yapılardan kuantum sonrası kafes varsayımlarına
abstract: Digital signature schemes are indispensable cryptographic primitives for ensuring au- thenticity, integrity, and non-repudiation in modern communication systems. Aggre- gate signatures and multi-signatures improve the efficiency of digital signatures by reducing communication, storage, and verification costs in distributed environments such as blockchain, cloud computing, and the Internet of Things. However, exist- ing verification algorithms require processing all signed messages or all participating signers, which causes the verification cost to grow linearly with the size of the system. In order to overcome this limitation, the notion of local verifiability was introduced, enabling a verifier to efficiently verify the inclusion of a particular message in an ag- gregate signature through a compact auxiliary value without requiring access to the complete message set. Although this concept opened up a new research direction, it remained largely restricted to message-oriented verification and classical crypto- graphic constructions. This thesis investigates local verifiability in aggregate and multi-signature schemes and presents a series of constructions that progressively extend its applicability from pairing-based settings to post-quantum lattice-based cryptography. First, a locally verifiable aggregate signature construction is proposed that supports the simultane- ous verification of multiple selected messages, allowing a verifier to validate multiple messages using a single auxiliary opening while preserving compact aggregate signatures and provable security. Subsequently, the concept of local verifiability is transferred from the message domain to the signer domain through the design of lo- cally verifiable multi-signature schemes, enabling efficient verification of the partic- ipation of individual signers without requiring verification over the complete signer set. The proposed techniques are then extended to a locally verifiable aggregated multi-signature scheme supporting dynamic signer participation, allowing different subsets of signers to jointly authorize multiple messages while preserving efficient aggregation and local verification. All three pairing-based constructions are proven unforgeable in the random oracle model: the first under Diffie–Hellman inversion assumptions, and the two multi-signature constructions under the computational co- Diffie–Hellman assumption with respect to honestly generated openings. Motivated by the transition toward post-quantum cryptography, this thesis extends local verifi- ability to lattice-based assumptions and presents L-LVMS, the first locally verifiable multi-signature scheme built on standard lattice hardness. The construction augments the two-round lattice-based multi-signature scheme MS2 with a deterministic local opening mechanism that allows efficient verification of an individual signer’s par- ticipation. The original key generation algorithm, the signature algorithm, and the signature size remain unchanged. L-LVMS is proven existentially unforgeable under chosen-message attacks in the random oracle model, assuming honestly generated local openings, under the MSIS and MLWE assumptions together with the security of an underlying trapdoor homomorphic commitment scheme. The thesis further ex- amines the case of adversarially generated local openings and shows that this setting introduces fundamental limitations, motivating post-quantum succinct arguments as a direction for future work. Overall, this thesis presents a systematic progression of locally verifiable signature schemes. The concept is first developed for message-domain verification in clas- sical pairing-based constructions, then extended to signer-domain verification, and finally established under post-quantum lattice assumptions. The proposed construc- tions broaden the applicability of local verification, improve the efficiency and scala- bility of distributed signature systems. They also provide rigorous security guarantees under well-established cryptographic assumptions. In doing so, this thesis contributes to the development of practical and scalable locally verifiable signature schemes for both classical and post-quantum cryptographic settings.

title: Biologically plausible computations in the brain, deep learning, and artificial intelligence
abstract: Biologically plausible computations in the brain, deep learning, and artificial intelligenceOne of the key approaches that I have developed in the research described in this book is to complement the empirical discoveries in neuroscience described here on key brain systems with computational neuroscience approaches to understand not just what each brain system does, but how it performs the computations.Indeed, I see a key part of understanding the brain and human behavior as understanding the brain's computational systems, and how they interact.The approach that I take is to develop our computational understanding of real systems in the brain.My computational neuroscience approach is thus somewhat different from some approaches in theoretical neuroscience (Dayan and Abbott, 2001; Hertz, Krogh and Palmer, 1991; Gerstner, Kistler, Naud and Paninski, 2014; Izhikevich, 2007; Ermentrout and Terman, 2010), which seek to understand the computations that can be performed by neural systems theoretically, but frequently without applying this to understand directly what computations are performed by different cortical regions, and how each cortical region performs its computations.Indeed, I think that the approach of the computational neuroscience research described in this book is rather pioneering in developing computational neuroscience theories and models of what many cortical systems in the brain compute, and how they compute it.Given the importance of this computational neuroscience approach to understanding real neural systems in the brain, it then becomes of great interest to examine whether the principles of operation and computations performed by the brain (Rolls, 2016b, 2026d) are similar to how computations are performed in computers.This is especially timely now, for artificial intelligence (AI) approaches implemented on digital computers are being used by some as models of how the brain performs its computations, and this does need to be very carefully considered, as I show in this Chapter and in more detail elsewhere (Rolls, 2026d).Given this background, in this Chapter I describe comparisons I have developed (Rolls, 2023c(Rolls, , 2026d) ) between computations in the brain and computations performed in computers (Section 8.1).This is intended to be helpful to those engineers, computer scientists, AI specialists and others interested in designing new computers that emulate aspects of brain function.The comparison between computation in the brain and computation in computers in Section 8.1 is also intended to be of interest to neuroscientists to emphasize the differences in the implementations of computation in the brain and in digital computers, including digital computers when they are running artificial intelligence algorithms that involve deep learning in multilayer networks.Part of the interest here is that many computer implementations of 'neural networks' implement very different algorithms to those implemented in the brain.This means that there is a lot left not only to learn about the brain, but also to learn from the brain.For example, Section 8.2 specifically compares deep learning in artificial neural networks to the type of self-organising learning implemented in the brain.Section 8.3 considers the pioneering approach taken in Brain Computations and Connectivity (Rolls, 2023c), in Brain Computations and Principles; and AI (Rolls, 2026d), and in this book

title: Governed Agent Morphogenesis: Runtime Organizational Reconfiguration with Bounded Authority and Causal Continuity
abstract: Agent collectives may need to recruit specialists, transfer work, and retire participants during a mission. Such changes cross independently authoritative services and can leave material effects even when a competing proposal wins organizational commitment. We present a transition contract connecting an exact approved proposal, current owner authority, stable effect identities, accepted lineage, and explicit cleanup. A reference implementation separates successful completion from terminal supersession of a losing proposal. Reproducible PostgreSQL experiments exercise concurrent transitions, mandate expiry, lost acknowledgements, and retirement with admitted work. An adversarial admission matrix compares four controllers under identical owner enforcement; the durable workflow and Morphogenesis both reject invalid authority and preserve recoverable effects. A bounded TLA+ model checks successor uniqueness, stable effects and safe termination, with counterexamples for deliberately weakened variants. These results identify the integration obligations that make organizational reconfiguration inspectable and recoverable. Version 1.0. Reference implementation: AgentPlat 1.0.0. Reproducible evidence and original experiment sources: https://github.com/Agentplat/agentplat/tree/paper-v0.5/docs/research/morphogenesis-paper-v0.5 . The stable software release does not expand the bounded experimental claims. Author contact: douglas.rodriguez@trafilea.com

title: Evaluating the Robustness of Segmentation Models against Adversarial Patches in Off-Road Environments
abstract: Semantic Segmentation (SS) is critical for autonomous vehicles to navigate off-road environments by identifying drivable terrain. Although models like ResNet34+UNet and EfficientViT have been proposed for these tasks, their susceptibility to localized adversarial patches in unstructured environments remains under-researched. This paper presents a comprehensive robustness evaluation of six real-time SS architectures, including the state-of-the-art YOLOv11 and YOLOv12 segmentation variants against five diverse adversarial patch schemes. Our experiments, conducted on a modified YCOR dataset, demonstrate that EfficientViT is the most resilient architecture, maintaining high accuracy with minimal performance degradation. In contrast, single-stage models like YOLOv11n-seg exhibit significant vulnerability, with pixel accuracy drops reaching 26.55%. We also show how decreases in overall segmentation accuracy impact the segmentation models’ ability to discern traversable terrain from non-traversable terrain.

title: Space-Based Quantum Communications: A System-Level Review
abstract: Space-based quantum key distribution (QKD) has emerged as the leading approach for establishing information-theoretically secure communication links beyond the reach of terrestrial fiber networks. Over the past decade, missions ranging from the 635 kg Micius satellite to 3U CubeSats such as SpooQy-1 have demonstrated satellite-to-ground QKD, entanglement distribution, and quantum teleportation across distances exceeding 1,200 km. However, existing reviews of these missions focus primarily on quantum protocols and link layer physics, leaving the system level engineering trade offs particularly those governing platform selection, SWaP budgets, and subsystem integration largely unexamined. This paper presents a systems engineering review of space based quantum communication missions developed between 2016 and 2025. Each mission is analyzed through a unified framework encompassing link budget decomposition, payload miniaturization trends, and Acquisition, Tracking, and Pointing (ATP) architectures. A comparative SWaP analysis reveals that payload mass has decreased by approximately one order of magnitude from ~230 kg (Micius) to ~23 kg (Jinan-1) while reported quantum bit error rates have remained below 5%. The analysis identifies three critical gaps: (i) the absence of formal Multidisciplinary Design Optimization (MDO) frameworks in quantum satellite design, (ii) the lack of standardized performance metrics for cross mission comparison, and (iii) the disconnect between constellation level network studies and subsystem level hardware constraints. Based on these findings, system-level design strategies and a technology roadmap are proposed to support the transition from single-link demonstrations to scalable, constellation-ready quantum communication infrastructures.

title: Fine-tuning Embeddings for Register Classification Reveals Functional Subtypes within Social Media Registers
abstract: Registers are often treated as uniform text categories, although individual registers frequently exhibit systematic internal variation. We present a data-driven exploration of register subtypes within pre-established register categories by combining supervised multilingual register classification with unsupervised clustering. Using fine-tuned XLM-R models, we classify one million web documents in three languages (English, Finnish, and Swedish) into a 25-class register taxonomy. title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Corporate Finance
abstract: Abstract This chapter examines how artificial intelligence and machine learning are utilized in corporate finance research. It provides an overview of the applications and identifies three main goals for using machine learning in data analysis: (1) predicting independent variables or identifying variables that support predictions, (2) uncovering patterns in data, and (3) enhancing causal inferences. The chapter discusses how machine learning techniques are tailored to exploit large datasets, offering advantages when dealing with numerous variables, nonlinear relationships, and the need for out-of-sample predictive accuracy. The chapter also provides examples of machine learning applications for processing and utilizing unstructured data, allowing researchers to quantify constructs that have previously been difficult to capture in corporate finance research. Although applications in classic corporate finance fields remain scarce, the chapter outlines two promising examples: mergers and acquisitions and default prediction.
